_readme: THE HYPE WAVE - the seasonal battle pass, 08-progression.md §10.
FIFTY TIERS, ONE XP STREAM. The pass is fed by the same account XP a match and a
mission already pay (§10.1: 'No separate pass currency'). That is the whole reason
it is cheap to build and the whole reason its pacing has to be calibrated rather
than guessed - change what a match pays and you change how long a season takes.
WHY xpPerTier IS 750 AND NOT THE DESIGN'S 1,000. §10.4 derives its pacing from
§2.2's assumption that a match averages 75 XP. The shipped match pays 25, plus 15
for a win - the same re-scale the Mastery curve already carries, for the same
reason. What must stay true is not the XP but §10.4's RIGHTMOST COLUMN: the
Regular finishes in week 7, the Casual in week 8, the Lurker in week 10. Re-derived
against shipped numbers, 750 XP per tier lands all three exactly. tests/hypewave
recomputes this from the shipped constants, so changing match or mission XP without
re-scaling the tier cost fails immediately - which §10.6.8 requires ('this
calibration is a release-blocking test on data/progression.json values').
ONE DIFFERENCE FROM §10.4'S TABLE, STATED. Its models credit 200 XP for the first
win of the day; the shipped first-win bonus pays 30 Clout and no XP. The baselines
in the test are computed WITHOUT it, so the calibration measures the game that
exists rather than the one the table assumed.
SEASONS ARE DATA. Two are authored with explicit, contiguous dates. Adding a third
is a JSON entry plus a cosmetics block - no code. Between the last season's end and
whatever comes next, the pass says so honestly and the Archive Pass keeps paying.
NOTHING HERE EXPIRES. §10.6 is binding: no login streaks, no forfeiting, and an
unfinished pass becomes an Archive Pass that keeps progressing at half rate forever.
The screen shows 'ahead / on pace / Rebound active' and never a countdown.
_encoreNote: §10.1: past tier 50, every further tier's worth of XP pays this, endlessly.
_reboundNote: §10.5.1 Wave Rebound. The pace line is 5 tiers per completed season week; while
your tier is under it, pass XP is earned at +50%. It is automatic, it is never
announced as urgency, and it is the reason a player who misses two weeks is behind
_archiveNote: §10.5.3 Archive Pass. A season ending does not take an unfinished pass away: it
keeps earning 50% of everything until tier 50, forever, and the Backstage Pass can
still be bought and retro-claimed on it.
_welcomeBackNote: §10.5.4. The reduced form: the Clout and the forced Rebound week ship. The
pre-banked dailies and the extra weekly slot need the mission rotation to accept
granted missions, which it has no vocabulary for - see DEFERRED_PASS.
_fillerNote: §10.2: 'Every tier pays something (no dead tiers)'. A tier with no entry in the
tables below pays this on the free track. The Backstage track's filler is a minor
seasonal cosmetic, which has no system yet and is therefore listed as deferred
rather than granted - except the four card-back tints, which are real.
_freeNote: §10.2, verbatim. Because gameplay content must be free, every card, pack, wildcard
and Glimmer in the pass sits on THIS track. Two rows cannot be paid yet and say so:
tier 35's Event Variant and tier 50's animated card back both need a variant-art

_backstageNote: §10.3, and the honest half of it. The Backstage Pass is cosmetic-only by design,
and most of what §10.3 lists - leader skins, battlefields, animated portraits,
music packs, alternate-art Legendaries - needs a system this build does not have.
Those rows are kept so the track shows what it will be, and refused at grant time.
